To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mesocarnivorous species in the Stara Mountain Mountains (Bulgaria) exhibit spatio temporal partition in both the warm and the cold season; (2) the degree of niche overlap among species is related to their trophic niches and (3) seasonal changes in diet are important for niche overlap and spatio temporal niche partitioning among species.

the five mesocarnivorans in the Stara planina mountains, Bulgaria, showed clear temporal and spatial segregation of their activity and hunting patterns that were related to body size and dietary preferences.
the golden jackal and European badger were the largest and most similar mesocarnivorous species in the Stara Mountain range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatio temporal distribution and interactions between five species of mesocarnivorous mammals in the Stara Mountain, Bulgaria.
the ecological mechanisms that facilitate the sympatric co-existence of mesocarnivorous species in the Stara planina mountains in Bulgaria.
the spatio temporal niche partitioning of a mesocarnivorous guild in the Stara planina mountain range in Bulgaria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spatio temporal niche partitioning observed in this guild of mesocarnivorous species in the Stara planina mountains, Bulgaria is a result of both body size and dietary differences between species.

the mesocarnivorous guild in this study is able to coexist due to a combination of factors including spatial and temporal partitioning and the presence of a large number of potential prey items, which is likely to be the case in many other areas.
the spatio temporal segregation of the species is a consequence of the niche variation hypothesis, but also the fact that all species have similar diets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the niche variation hypothesis appears to be supported by our data, and that spatio temporal partitioned niche overlap may facilitate coexistence in mesocarnivorous species.
spatio temporal partition is a mechanism that facilitates sympatry between mesocarnivorous species in the Stara planina mountain range.
the niche variation hypothesis is supported for the mesocarnivorous guild in the Stara Mountain, Bulgaria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of strong competition and/or habitat fragmentation, mesocarnivorous species may persist sympatrically, even in the face of similar dietary niche requirements.

the spatio temporal niche variation hypothesis can be applied to mesocarnivorous species, and that it is a powerful mechanism for facilitating coexistence in a region with relatively low species richness.
mesocarnivorous mammals can coexist in sympatry by utilizing different temporal and spatial resources.
